title: Formation palette: does one of these read as crystal?
question: You said 'nothing here looks like a crystal'. One of these gives formations their own material with a designed palette. Does either read as crystal/stone-formation to you now — and if neither does, is it the colour that is still wrong or purely the shape?
context_md:
Phase 0 of the overnight plan, canyon seed 1 at 8x, same cave and same seed both sides.

**What changed.** Speleothems used to be written as `stone`/`crystal` — literally the same material id as the cave wall, told apart only by a palette shade. They now have their own materials (`flowstone`, `spar`), which is what lets them be walk-through scenery while the wall stays a wall.

**The palette is the part I want judged.** Crystal's four tones are luma ~205, 224, 240, 250 — *all four inside the top fifth of the range* — so an object drawn in them has no internal edge and reads flat whatever silhouette you give it. That is why brightening it earlier made things worse, not better. The new palettes span 96–214 (`flowstone`) and 84–252 (`spar`), each with a **darkest tone below the surrounding rock**, so a formation has somewhere to shade *to*.

**What has NOT changed, so please ignore it:** the shape. These are still 1–2 cells wide with no taper. Fewer/thicker/tapered is the next track's job and I deliberately did not relax the 'never bridge floor to ceiling' rule yet, because doing that without the taper makes *more* one-cell columns, not fewer.

**Also in but not visible here:** the gnome now walks through formations and can still mine them (two tests, both confirmed able to fail — turning the flag off fails the walk-through one with 'he stalled at x=57.4').
